🇲🇽✊ "How could there not be unity between people and government? Because we deliver, because we do not betray, because we do not lie, we do not steal and we do not betray the people of Chiapas or the people of Mexico." — Presidenta Claudia Sheinbaum, Tuxtla Gutiérrez, Chiapas Closing the housing event in Tuxtla Gutiérrez on November 8, she answered those who "can't explain" the government's popular support: 13 million older adults receive their pension, 3 million women aged 60 to 64 receive the Mujeres Bienestar pension, more than 500,000 farmers are in Sembrando Vida, all people with disabilities receive support, 2 million small producers get free fertilizer, and the debts of 5 million people were settled or restructured — plus housing, hydroelectric plants, trains and highways.

text: 🔥🇲🇽 "Explain to me how, with a credit of 104,000, you pay and pay and pay and pay, and you owe one million pesos. Pure usury, pure swindle, pure robbery." — Presidenta Claudia Sheinbaum, Tuxtla Gutiérrez, Chiapas At the Los Poetas housing handover in Tuxtla on November 8, she read out real Infonavit cases from the neoliberal period. Francisco Toledo borrowed 79,000 pesos, paid 231,000 and still owed 173,000. Patricia Cervantes borrowed 104,000, paid 338,000 — more than three times the loan — and owed 1,132,000. Both now owe zero. Fovissste also returned overpayments to borrowers. She said Infonavit used to give 40 m² homes two hours from where people lived, on credits "that never finished being paid." More than 5 million such loans have been restructured.

🇲🇽✊ "Before there were 30 requirements. You had to add up 1,080 points. Nobody could, or almost nobody, and when they reached it, what they were given wasn't enough to buy the home." — Octavio Romero Oropeza, Director of Infonavit, Tuxtla Gutiérrez, Chiapas On Sheinbaum's instruction — "we have to simplify, we have to help people" — Infonavit dropped all of them. Three conditions remain: be a contributor, earn between 1 and 2.9 minimum wages, and not own a home. Of the 50,000 people who have already received a home: 75% are young, 91% earn 1 to 1.5 minimum wages, 53% are women. The 400 homes at Los Poetas in Tuxtla sold out in 3 days. Nationally Infonavit has 593,000 of its 1.2 million homes contracted and 260,000 under construction. In Chiapas, 45,000 families had "unpayable" loans restructured and 44,000 paid-off mortgages are being released free of charge, a procedure that used to cost 16,000 to 18,000 pesos.

🇲🇽✊ "It is not the same, 5% of 80 pesos as 5% of 248." — Octavio Romero Oropeza, Director of Infonavit, Tuxtla Gutiérrez, Chiapas Employers pay 5% of each worker's wage into Infonavit's housing fund. López Obrador took the daily minimum wage from 80 to 248 pesos; Sheinbaum followed with raises of 12% and 13%. Romero said the fund held 140 billion pesos when López Obrador arrived, 780 billion when he left, and holds 1.14 trillion today. That money now finances construction directly, so builders no longer load bank interest into the price. With federal, state and municipal fee waivers and builders accepting smaller margins, homes worth over 1.2 million pesos — at least 60 m², two bedrooms — are delivered for a little over half their cost to workers earning 1 to 2.9 minimum wages.

🇲🇽✊ "What governments do, if we are good governments, is help the people. The effort is yours. We facilitate, we help fulfill something that is a right of the people of Mexico: access to housing, access to education, access to health, a good wage, being able to open a small business. That is what governments that love the people do. And if there is one thing that characterizes the governments of the Fourth Transformation, it is that we love the people of Mexico." — Presidenta Claudia Sheinbaum, Tuxtla Gutiérrez, Chiapas On November 8 she handed over 55 Infonavit apartments at the Los Poetas housing development in Tuxtla Gutiérrez, plus 311 Fovissste mortgage-settlement certificates. The Vivienda para el Bienestar program aims at 1.8 million homes for low-income families; 5 million families have had their Infonavit or Fovissste debts restructured. Counting deeds and new credits, she said 12 million families will benefit in total.

🇲🇽🏭 <u>US Tariffs Hit Cars That Are 40% American-Made</u>

US imports of passenger cars from Mexico fell 20% in January–July 2026 compared with the same period of 2024, even as total imports from Mexico rose nearly 24%, El Economista reports. CSIS researcher Diego Marroquín Bitar told the US International Trade Commission that "Mexican vehicles incorporate, on average, around 40% US components," far more than cars from other markets. He warned that tightening T-MEC rules of origin "would start raising costs and displacing production outside North America."

🇲🇽🚆 <u>Delfina Gómez Puts Edomex Highway Concessionaires on Notice</u>

State of Mexico Governor Delfina Gómez is reviewing every highway concession granted under public-private partnership (APP) and long-term service (PPS) contracts. Companies that failed to maintain their roads will lose them. Concessionaires let Periférico Norte, Periférico Oriente, Paseo Tollocan and Avenida Las Torres fall apart, so the state's own road agency had to step in. It has already rehabilitated 1,638 km in the biggest road-rescue program in four decades.
